assets.content:
Subject: Got ahead on posts, then today happens
Preview text: Drag the new one to the front of your queue and the rest shift down, no rewriting.

Hi there,

You run your own social, and some weeks you'd rather not do it live every day.

Buffer is social media software that holds your planned posts in a queue, in the order they'll go out — Facebook and Instagram among them.

When something happens in the shop, you add a post and drag it to the front, and the rest shift down instead of being rewritten.

That's how Foster Coffee Company works it: far enough ahead that they're not scrambling to find content, yet free to click and drag in a last-minute post when the day calls for one.

On the Free plan you line up 10 scheduled posts per channel at a time — so ten each for Facebook and Instagram — and paid plans are unlimited. The plans page confirms exactly what's included, so it's worth a look before you start a weekly queue.

See our plans and pricing →

- the Buffer team

emails.felt_need: Local business clients are often too busy to post to their own social media accounts themselves.
emails.status_quo: Local business clients working with a local SEO/marketing agency either handle their own organic social posting or hand that task off to someone else entirely.
emails.why_it_fails: A fixed plan and a timely update pull in opposite directions: stay ahead and you can't react; stay reactive and you never get ahead.
emails.mechanism: Buffer holds your planned posts in a queue in the order they'll go out, and you rearrange them by clicking and dragging — so when something timely comes up, you add it and the rest shift down instead of being rewritten. On the Free plan you can line up 10 scheduled posts per channel at a time (paid plans are unlimited).
emails.belief_shift: Before: planning ahead and leaving room for a timely update are opposites. After: a queue lets you do both — line up the week and still drop in today's news.
must_not_say: Do not claim or imply Buffer increases organic reach or visibility
Do not state or imply any quantified time saving (no 'save X hours')
Do not claim Buffer supports every social channel; Facebook and Instagram may appear only as examples
Do not promise to fix low organic reach
Do not mention a knowledge base / RAG capability or reusable per-client agent configuration
Do not cite the 30% follower-growth figure — it reads as a reach/growth claim the request forbids
Do not claim Knowledge base / RAG context; its capability state is unknown.
Do not claim Reusable per-client agent configuration; its capability state is unknown.
emails.tone: Clear, encouraging and practical, with a touch of low-key warmth — the way Buffer's own help copy reads.
emails.call_to_action: Learn more about our plans and pricing here (review the official Free plan)
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether the Free plan's 10-posts-per-channel limit is enough to run a weekly queue before signing up.
emails.next_step_value: The official page lets the reader confirm exactly what the Free plan includes, including the 10 scheduled posts per channel limit, before committing.
emails.next_step_limit: Reviewing the plan page does not set up the queue itself or connect a channel — that happens after sign-up.
emails.subject_strategy: Name the tension the reader feels — getting posts ready ahead without losing room for today's local news — so the open promises the exact problem the email resolves.

brief.voice_notes: Use 'you' and 'Buffer'; short, direct sentences. Echo the reader's own framing ('a few posts ahead', 'something happening in the shop'). State the Free plan limit as a plain fact, not a warning.
